ostrzezenia.tekst: Pressure canning is the only recommended method for canning meat, poultry, seafood and vegetables; using a boiling-water bath for these foods poses a real risk of botulism poisoning. [T:SZY-006]
NCHFP recommends canning low-acid foods, and tomatoes and tomato products, only according to the procedures in the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning. [T:SZY-007]
According to NCHFP, butter or ghee should not be added to jars, even with liquid, in research-based processes if the original instructions do not call for them. [T:SZY-013]

akapity: Most mixtures of low-acid and acid foods are also low-acid, unless the recipe has enough lemon juice, citric acid or vinegar to make them acid foods. [T:SZY-002]
JarAtlas does not treat a dish as an acid food because it tastes sour, or because acid was added without a tested recipe. [T:-]
JarAtlas has found no tested home recipe for canned onion stifado from a checked source. [T:-]
JarAtlas applies the same rule to oil and other fats: they should not be added to jars unless a tested recipe calls for them. [T:-]
